task.text: Make flaky calls recover on their own, without hammering the dependency.

Implement `Retry` (constructor given). Time and randomness are injected: it sleeps through a `Sleeper` and picks each delay with the `LongUnaryOperator jitter`, which maps a ceiling in ms to the delay in ms.

items: `long ceilingMs(int attempt)`: for a 1-based attempt, `min(capMs, baseMs * 2^(attempt-1))`. It must not overflow for large attempts.
`<T> T call(Supplier<T> op)` runs `op`, retrying only on `TransientException`, up to `maxAttempts` calls in total.
Between attempts sleep `jitter.applyAsLong(ceilingMs(attempt))` ms. Never sleep after the last attempt.
When attempts run out, rethrow the last `TransientException`. Any other exception, including `PermanentException`, propagates at once.

checks.title: Ceilings double and stop at the cap
Transient failures are retried with backoff
Each sleep is the jittered delay

hints.text: Two separate ideas: the *ceiling* grows deterministically, the *delay* is whatever the injected jitter picks below it. Keep them in two steps.
`call` is a loop over attempts. Catch `TransientException` only; if it is the last attempt rethrow, otherwise ask `jitter` for a delay and hand it to `sleeper`. Cap the shift so `<<` cannot overflow.
